long_biography.plain_text:
Property developer Lars-Erik Magnusson began by trading construction equipment in Sweden. A warehouse built for his own business became his first property sale, and he increasingly concentrated on buying and developing buildings. He later moved to the Netherlands, attracted by commercial property he considered undervalued.

His redevelopment of Amsterdam’s former head post office became Magna Plaza. The project required replacement of a decaying foundation and extensive rebuilding inside the historic shell, with new atriums and an enlarged glass roof bringing daylight into the shopping centre. When recession made tenants scarce, his company opened franchise shops itself to fill the building for its opening. He also pressed for Sunday trading, taking the proposal to Amsterdam’s mayor and city council.
long_biography.html:
Property developer Lars-Erik Magnusson began by trading construction equipment in Sweden. A warehouse built for his own business became his first property sale, and he increasingly concentrated on buying and developing buildings. He later moved to the Netherlands, attracted by commercial property he considered undervalued.

His redevelopment of Amsterdam’s former head post office became Magna Plaza. The project required replacement of a decaying foundation and extensive rebuilding inside the historic shell, with new atriums and an enlarged glass roof bringing daylight into the shopping centre. When recession made tenants scarce, his company opened franchise shops itself to fill the building for its opening. He also pressed for Sunday trading, taking the proposal to Amsterdam’s mayor and city council.
